correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, each pair of consecutive labelled configurations corresponds bijectively to a path in a fully specified 256-state transfer graph. The 400 allowed middle triples and 36 boundary pair entries are exhaustively enumerated. Exact integer evaluation proves p(T)e=0 (256 coordinates) with p=(z²−3z+1)(z³−1), and q(T_f)e_f=0 (256 coordinates) with q=(z−1)(z²−z−1), plus initial values; this is an exact finite certificate implying both recurrences for all n, not a finite-sample induction. A separate Lyapunov descent for a symmetric matrix with endpoint self-weights proves that higher periods are impossible. Brute-force simulation of all 87,376 binary states for 2<=n<=8 independently agrees. Quantifiers, endpoint tie normalization, labelled-orbit division by two, and asymptotics were checked. Code and its actual output are included in this row.

originality.rationale: Statement-level comparisons with the retrieved published-finding corpus hits, accessible prior claims, and relevant primary literature show no theorem implying the exact open-ladder P_n/Q_n counts or the n mod 3 correction. value.rationale: This is a complete, exact two-row strip dynamical census, a motivated step beyond single-row majority and qualitative finite-graph period bounds. It yields natural labelled invariants for every length, explicit numbers of primitive two-cycles, a nontrivial n mod 3 spatial resonance, and sharply different exponential scales for fixed versus period-two states. It is not an arbitrary finite slice or a routine restatement of the general period-two theorem. No attraction-basin claim is made.
